facts.fact: The World Bank's Nigeria Development Update says the identity of cash transfer recipients is validated through the National Identification Number (NIN) or Bank Verification Number (BVN) before payment.

NGA.note: Document says nothing on civil register and ID links.

facts.fact: The World Bank reports 4.4 million households had received at least one tranche of the federal government cash transfer paid directly into bank accounts, and 0.8 million a second, as of 8 October 2024.
The World Bank says payments to recipients' bank accounts are made after validating individuals through the NIN or BVN, and low NIN/BVN coverage among the poor slowed the rollout.

NGA.note: No count or share of people holding a national ID is given.
Document says nothing on ID numbers at birth.
Document says nothing on who operates the ID system.
No register is stated to be keyed on the ID number; only payment validation.
Document says nothing on the ID system's issuance, biometrics or certification.
No programme management information system is named.
